summary: Active optatives have God as subject and either a suffixal recipient, an overt plural NP (MAC NE Interview 2/48), or coordinated recipients (MAC Hanna Dewo/123). Detransitive blessings promote the blessed person to subject and do not necessarily announce a death.

mḥase as masculine Detransitive Preterit reports death; miḥase/miḥasən/miḥasyo are optative Infectum; mḥasyo/mḥasayto/mḥasye can describe a blessed/deceased state. Feminine finite mḥasyo overlaps the masculine Part. Pass. form; syntax and temporal anchoring matter.

The repeated reader claim that the Detransitive sense field contains ḥṣy III 'shut' is not borne out by this supplied entry: detransitiveSenses is empty and the intended gloss is combined under active sense 1. No unrelated text is deleted.

The Classical Syriac hymn at 66/279 is explicit register switching. It supports the religious semantic background but is excluded as Turoyo form evidence. Variants ḥasay/mḥase/mḥasay and s/ṣ are retained without normalizing the edition.
86/1 and prs 197/33 can be parallel attestations attached to one quoted example. Their different wording does not alone prove a bad citation; no reference is removed.
